//: THE WEAPON BENCH: give a soldier a weapon, put an enemy at a chosen distance, fire N shots, and hand back where every projectile actually LANDED - hits, misses, damage, and the dispersion of the group. The tracers are real, so a human can just watch it too.
//control: The honesty check: the SAME run with '{"setSpread":true,"spread":0}' must cluster far tighter than the stock-spread run. If it does not, the numbers are not measuring the weapon.
//needs: a tactical mission that is PLAYING, with one of YOUR soldiers selected - that soldier is the shooter.
//los: The enemy position is drawn at RANDOM from the distance band, so it can land behind cover and the plan then FAILS at assert-target ('the predicate was still false'). That is the validity check working, not a defect: re-run, or move the band. `seed` makes the draw reproducible.
//shooter: `shooter` is any `call` target: @selected (default), or a handle. NOT BUILT: this plan does not SPAWN the shooter. Spawn one first with plans\spawn-at-coordinate.json and select it if the mission has none - one 20-step spawn body inlined here is already the bulk of this file, and a second would be a copy of a plan that exists.
//out-of-turn: MEASURED, and the answer is that NO turn handling is needed. Three runs with the ALIEN faction on turn all reported abilityState NotDisabled, fired, and recorded their impacts: nothing in TacticalAbility.Activate (:1078-1122) gates on the current faction, and nothing here has to end a turn first. The one real consequence is that @selected is NULL during another faction's turn, so pass an explicit shooter handle then (get @faction.Actors, page it, take a TacticalActor).
//ammo: No ammoDef var: TacticalItem.ReloadForFree (TacticalItem.cs:830-848) is the game's own fill-to-max and handles BOTH shapes - it loads magazines of CompatibleAmmunition[0] when the item has an AmmoManager and calls SetChargesToMax when it does not. `equip-actor.json` adds an item and never loads one, which is why a weapon from it cannot fire.
//spread: weapon_spread multiplies the cone in Weapon.SpreadInCone (Weapon.cs:481). Left ALONE unless setSpread is true, and restored in `finally`.
//god_mode: MUST stay false. TacticalActorBase.ApplyDamageInternal returns at :846 BEFORE the report, the event and the HP change, so god_mode silently zeroes the entire measurement. The enemy is kept alive with targetHp instead.

steps.//ORIGINALS: Read BEFORE anything is changed. `finally` puts each of them back.

steps.//: The enemy must neither act nor return fire, or it is not a bench (TacticalFaction.cs:106).
Not a precaution - a REQUIREMENT. See //god_mode above.
Reproducible dispersion. seed 0 means 'do not touch the RNG' - 0 is falsy, so the step is skipped.

steps.//WEAPON: Typed at WeaponDef, not ItemDef. equip-actor.json searches broad ItemDef and takes defs[0], which is why "PX_AssaultRifle" resolves to the ammo CLIP there.

steps.//: EXACTLY one, asserted from both sides. An ambiguous weapon name must be a named failure, never a silently different weapon than the one being measured.

steps.//PRELOAD: MANDATORY, and for BOTH defs. `spawn` runs its whole spawn inside the loading callback (TacticalDeployZone.cs:424 -> :409-423) and `give_item` preloads its item def the same way (TacConsoleGameplay.cs:770). Skip it and the enemy comes up with no model - or the weapon with no tracer, which is the thing this plan exists to show.

steps.//RANGE: distance +/- tolerance, computed with Unity's own operators - the plan engine has no arithmetic and does not need any (the aim-and-run.json idiom).

steps.//SEARCH: spawn-squad.json's proven candidate search, inlined - a plan may not run a plan (Plan.cs:478). Keep the two in step.

steps.//: The search may run out of passes. FAILING here rather than relaxing the distance is the point: a bench that quietly measured 6 m when it was asked for 10 is worse than one that refuses.
ACHIEVED, not requested. Reported either way and asserted against the band.

steps.//TARGET HP: Keeps the target alive for the volley, and NOTHING MORE - hpBefore/hpAfter are not the damage measurement. MEASURED: the game recomputes a stat from its base plus its modifications, so a raised Health.Max does not stay raised; a live run set 5000, read 5000 back, and finished at 77 - the def's own max minus 63 damage. `damageTotal` is the authoritative figure: it is the sum the game itself accumulated per projectile, and in a clean run it reconciled EXACTLY with the HP delta (23+33+23+24 = 103 = 5000 -> 4897). SetMax then SetToMax, NOT the Set(float,bool) that set_infinite_ap uses (ACE_InfiniteAP.cs:34-35): StatusStat OVERRIDES BaseStat.Set with the identical signature (StatusStat.cs:86 / BaseStat.cs:95), so `call` scores the two equal and refuses as ambiguous - and `sig` cannot break that tie, because the parameter types are the same on both. SetToMax (StatusStat.cs:114) is declared once and reaches the same value.

steps.//EQUIP: The post-spawn path (equip-actor.json). AddItem does no capacity or slot check (InventoryComponent.cs:95-104) - the weapon lands in hand.

steps.//SELECT: MEASURED, not a precaution: without it the ability reports EquipmentNotSelected and nothing fires. AddItem puts the weapon in the actor's hands but leaves whatever was already selected selected (EquipmentComponent.cs:242). TacticalAbility.Activate would select it itself (:1087-1090) - but every enabledness check happens BEFORE that, so the bench would refuse a shot that is actually takeable.

steps.//AMMO: See //ammo. A weapon with zero charges reports IsEnabled false and fires nothing.

steps.//AP: Headless. set_infinite_ap works off the SELECTION (ACE_InfiniteAP.cs:27) and would need a cursor; this is the same two calls on the same stat.

steps.//ABILITY: TacticalActor.GetDefaultShootAbility(weapon) (:873) - the ability whose Source IS this weapon. A `wait` rather than a read: the ability is created when the item is added and may not be there in the same frame.

steps.//: GetDisabledState, NOT IsEnabled. IsEnabled is declared on BOTH Ability (:29) and TacticalAbility (:367) with the same one-parameter signature, so the binder scores them equal and refuses as ambiguous - and `sig` cannot break the tie, because the parameter types are identical. GetDisabledState (:372) is declared once, and it NAMES the reason instead of returning a bare false.

AbilityDisabledState is NOT an enum - it is a struct whose only field is a string Key (AbilityDisabledState.cs:7,163), and its ToString() localises through the shared data. So the readable answer is the Key, and comparing it is a plain string compare.

steps.//TARGET: ShootAbility.GetAttackActorTarget (:348) -> Weapon.TryGetShootTarget. A NULL here means the shot is not takeable at all - no line of sight, out of range - and that is the validity check, so it is asserted rather than passed on.

steps.//VOLLEY: `times` must be a LITERAL - Repeat reads args before substitution (Plan.cs:507-510), so "times":"${shots}" would silently mean 1. 20 is the hard ceiling; `shots` is honoured by the while guard.

steps.//: The bar for THIS shot: Shots.Landed counts impacts since the mark.

steps.//FIRE: ExecuteAndWait, and NOT Activate. Activate is declared on Ability (:34), TacticalAbility (:1078) AND ShootAbility (:152) with the identical (object) signature, so `call` refuses it as an ambiguous overload and no `sig` can break the tie. ExecuteAndWait (TacticalAbility.cs:1168) is declared once, calls Activate itself, and returns a plain NextUpdate - so it needs no Timing pump. Execute (:1159) is an ITERATOR: calling it through `call` would only build the state machine and never run a shot.

steps.//PACING:
The PROJECTILE is the pacing signal, because it is the only positive one that is actually true. Two alternatives were tried live and both are dead ends, recorded so nobody tries them again:
  - ActionComponent.HasPlayingActions(ActorActions, []) (ActionComponent.cs:164) counts NotStarted as well as Playing, which looks perfect - but IdleAbility sits on that same channel permanently (TacticalActorBase.HasExecutingAbilities at :699 explicitly filters it out), so the predicate is NEVER false and every shot timed out.
  - the ability's own IsExecuting is false while a shot is merely ENQUEUED (ShootAbility.cs:173 takes the EnqueueAction path for a Regular shot), so on its own it passes instantly. Each enqueue is soloAfterCurrent, and PlayActionAfterCurrent CANCELS everything already queued (ActionComponent.cs:80-91) - so a volley paced on it fires six activations in under a second and loses most of them.
Shots.Landed goes non-zero exactly when this shot's projectile reaches its terminal impact, which is the event being measured.

steps.//: ...and the tail of the action, so the next enqueue cannot cancel it. Near-instant once the projectile has landed; it is the cheap half of the pair, not the load-bearing one.
The aim point for the dispersion figures is where the enemy actually STANDS, read fresh.

finally.//: The observer FIRST: a patch left armed keeps writing into a ring nobody is reading.

MANDATORY. A run that dies with the AI off leaves the mission unplayable to a human, and one that dies with weapon_spread at 0 leaves every weapon in the save laser-accurate. god_mode is written back to false rather than to GOD0 because the plan only ever forces it to false.
The enemy and the weapon STAY. Watching the tracers is half the point, and deleting the situation the bench just built is a separate decision.
